profile.what: Bosch Ltd (formerly Motor Industries Co., MICO) is the listed Indian flagship of Robert Bosch GmbH, which owns 70.54% (Jun-2026). Three reported segments: Automotive Products (Rs17,807 cr in FY26, 89% of revenue: Power Solutions = diesel and gasoline fuel injection and engine management for cars, CVs, tractors and off-highway; 2-Wheeler & Powersports = engine management, sensors, ABS; Mobility Aftermarket = spares, filters, spark plugs, wipers, batteries, lubricants, workshop network), Consumer Goods (Rs1,836 cr: Bosch power tools, mostly traded from the group) and Others (Rs391 cr: building technology until its sale in May-2025, plus rental and services). Since Jul-2026 it also owns 100% of Bosch Chassis Systems India (RBIC: ABS, ESP, airbag control units, braking, Rs3,936 cr revenue in FY25).
profile.employees: Bosch Group in India: 38,655 associates at Mar-2025, 17 manufacturing sites (group); Bosch Ltd plants at Bengaluru (Adugodi), Naganathapura, Bidadi, Nashik, Jaipur, Gangaikondan, Chennai; RBIC at Chakan, Manesar, Sanand

shares.note: 2,460 shares allotted on 10-Jun-2026 to Robert Bosch Investment Nederland and Robert Bosch LLC at Rs35,200 as part payment for RBIC (locked in to 30-Jan-2028).

rbic.proforma: FY25 pro forma: revenue Rs22,023 cr (+22%), EBITDA Rs3,068 cr (13.9% vs 12.8%), EPS Rs720 vs Rs683 (+5%)
rbic.timeline: Board approval 8-Apr-2026; shareholders approved by postal ballot 8-May-2026 (related-party vote: promoters cannot vote); shares allotted 10-Jun-2026; sale completed in Jul-2026; consolidated from Q2FY27 (MD, 11-Aug-2026). No goodwill or amortisation (common-control transaction).

rbic.customers: Tata Motors, Maruti Suzuki, Toyota, Bajaj Auto (awards listed in the deck)
rbic.royalty: Royalty and transfer pricing for RBIC 'very similar' to Bosch Ltd (CFO, 13-Apr-2026)

callPoints: Revenue Rs5,842 cr (+22%): Power Solutions +29% (cars, off-highway, tractors; 'volume effect and some new introductions'), 2-Wheeler +41% (EMS content, premium motorcycle platforms, share gains), aftermarket +9.6% (independent aftermarket had its best month ever in June), power tools +21%.

EBITDA margin 14.0% (+65bp): gross margin fell ~420bp to 33.5% (more traded goods, commodities), offset by lower employee and other costs. MD: 'we are on an upward trend, and we would say that we will sustain this'; no one-offs in employee or other expenses.
PAT Rs702 cr standalone (Rs706 cr consolidated), -37% YoY because Q1FY26 held the Rs556 cr gain on the building-technology sale; +9.9% excluding it.
RBIC: 'The sale was completed in July'; consolidation from Q2; no goodwill or amortisation; minimal cost synergies; analyst visit to Chakan planned for November.
Industry: ~8% growth expected next quarter; GST-related normalisation 'maybe in 1 or 2 more quarters'; exports ~8-8.5% of revenue, to rise.

Regulation: CAFE Phase 3 (draft) from Apr-2027 and CV ADAS from Jan-2027 (new models) / Oct-2027 (all) are content opportunities; the Tata AutoComp e-axle JV should have revenue by late next year; the TSF air-systems JV starts customer talks from Sep-2026.
New CFO: Tillmann Olsen's first call (Karin Gilges signed the FY26 accounts).

guidance.said: 'We believe we will hold margins very steady for the next 5 years or so'; order book 'very, very full' with projects funded to launch in 2031.
guidance.outcome: Consolidation begins Q2FY27 (after our as-of date)

guidance.said: 'Even after the deal well equipped with cash'; Rs9,000 cr equity value includes RBIC's own cash; both companies debt free.
'Cautiously optimistic... we currently maintained a flattish outlook' because of the West Asia conflict and oil prices; market prognosis 26.9-28.3 mn vehicles in FY27 (FY26 26.86 mn).
Established mid-2026; first shipments from the JV in Q3 of calendar 2027.
Current EBITDA margin sustainable: localisation, productivity, mix, global purchasing.
~8-8.5% of revenue today; aim to raise it over the next few years.

history.what: Motor Industries Co. (MICO) incorporated in Bengaluru (CIN ...1951PLC000761); manufacturing in India since 1953
history.impact: Grew up as Bosch's Indian maker of diesel fuel-injection systems; Robert Bosch GmbH now owns 70.54%

history.what: Year-end moved from December to March: a 15-month FY15
history.impact: FY15 numbers are not comparable; our charts start FY16

history.what: Share buybacks: shares fell from 3.14 cr (FY16) to 2.95 cr (FY19)
history.impact: Cash returned besides dividends; Screener financing outflows Rs2,670 cr (FY17) and Rs2,531 cr (FY19)

history.what: BS-VI emission norms: diesel cars shrank, Bosch's diesel-heavy content per vehicle reset
history.impact: FY20-FY21 revenue fell 19% and 1%; EBITDA margin 15% then 12%
Rs645 cr and Rs745 cr exceptional charges; reported EPS Rs220 and Rs163

history.what: Project House Mobility Solutions business sold to group company Bosch Mobility Platform and Solutions India for Rs781 cr; Rs59 cr restructuring provision reversed
history.impact: Rs844 cr exceptional gain; reported EPS Rs845 vs Rs625 before it

history.what: OE/OES diagnosis business sold to group company ETAS Automotive India (Rs45.6 cr); new Rs47 cr restructuring provision
Video, access, intrusion and communication systems (building technologies) sold to Keenfinity India for Rs595 cr
history.impact: Rs556 cr exceptional gain; reported EPS Rs940 vs Rs796 before it; 'Others' segment revenue halves

history.what: Two 50:50 JVs: e-axles and motors with Tata AutoComp (Nashik); electronic air systems for trucks and buses with the TSF Group (Brakes India, Wheels India)
history.impact: Equity-accounted; revenue from late 2027; investment amounts not quantified by the company in our sources

history.what: RBIC (Vehicle Motion) bought from the parent for Rs9,068.68 cr, 99.9% cash
history.impact: ~+25% revenue, margin accretive; uses ~two-thirds of the treasury, so other income falls

dividendPolicy: Endeavour to pay 55-85% of PAT (excluding special dividends), up to 100%; FY26 payout was only 29% (Rs270 final) with cash kept for RBIC. Repeated in the RBIC deck ('committing to dividend distribution of 55% to 85% of PAT').
